title: When I start a pull request that requires additional review steps, I want to use custom checklists a
job_to_be_done: When I start a pull request that requires additional review steps, I want to use custom checklists and approval gates within GitHub, so I can avoid lost context and missed review deadlines.
painful_workflow: Creating issues linked to PRs, manually tracking review status in spreadsheets, or using external tools like Asana or Jira because GitHub's built-in review workflow doesn't support custom checklists, approval gates, or cross-repo reviews.
current_workaround: Creating issues linked to PRs, manually tracking review status in spreadsheets, or using external tools like Asana or Jira.
verified_facts: A single search-derived signal (SIG-0003, source SRC-0003) claims GitHub's built-in review workflow lacks custom checklists, approval gates, and cross-repo review support.
The same single signal claims the workaround is linked issues, spreadsheets, or external tools (Asana/Jira), occurring 'daily, per PR'.
The cluster has exactly 1 independent source and 1 source type.
inferences: PRs occur daily in active development teams, so the trigger event is plausibly frequent — but the painful subset is unquantified.
Teams using Jira/Asana as a workaround already pay for those tools for other reasons, so the marginal workaround cost is likely low.
The pain pattern, if real, would apply globally because GitHub usage is not jurisdiction-specific.
assumptions: That the claimed consequences (lost context, missed deadlines, duplicate work) actually occur at meaningful scale — asserted but not evidenced.

That GitHub's native features (branch protection required reviews, required status checks, PR template task lists, GitHub Projects) do not adequately mitigate the gap — the evidence never engages with them.
That team leads, rather than the org's existing PM tooling owner, would be the buyer.
unknowns: No user quotes, forum threads, feature-request upvotes, or community discussion evidence.
No quantification: team sizes affected, time lost per PR, cost of missed deadlines.
No willingness-to-pay data: no existing paid solution spend, no budget owner identified.
No competitive landscape: whether existing review-tooling products already solve this and at what adoption.
No analysis of how GitHub-native features (branch protection, CODEOWNERS, Projects, PR templates) partially cover the claimed gap.
No segmentation: does this affect 5-person startups, regulated enterprises, or open-source maintainers differently?
